docs/content/1.guide/0.why.md.skeleton: I started {0}i18n-ally{/0} in 2019. Since then, I have always dreamed of a standalone core for i18n support, with a CLI and a language server on top, so it would be more general and easier to use in wider environments, not only in VS Code. But i18n-ally had grown inside the VS Code API, and as it moved to Lokalise and I moved on to other projects, the idea stayed on my list.

Agents make that possible. A rewrite of this size used to need months, and now I can build it in my free time and still make it solid. Agents also would benefit from it: they edit locale files all day, and they need the key behind a text, the missing keys and a safe way to rename a key. So I brought the idea back, and this time I made it real.

If you ever enjoyed i18n-ally, x18n is a more powerful and a lot more robust version of it, and I highly recommend that you {0}migrate{/0}. If you have never used it, give it a try with {1}Getting started{/1}.
